about: Size ceilings for the study records the dashboard downloads at startup: data/demographics.part1..N.json.gz.

part_count is the number of parts app.js fetches (NUM_PARTS). part_gzip_max_bytes is a per-file budget and total_gzip_max_bytes a budget for the sum over the parts; neither is a hosting limit. The parts are served from GitHub Pages, and the hard limits are GitHub's: a file over 100 MiB cannot be pushed, and a Pages site over 1 GB cannot be published.

The ceilings ratchet down: each engine change that shrinks the parts is followed by a site change lowering them to the new size plus about 15% headroom, so a weekly push cannot quietly grow them back.

The engine's weekly publish (scripts/check_site_contract.py in civicsample-engine) reads this file before pushing. For size it warns over budget and still pushes, and blocks only at the hard limits; a part count other than part_count blocks the push. tests/data_budget.test.mjs checks the committed parts against this file and fails when they are over budget: the alarm on the site side, after the push is live. CI runs it on main and on every site pull request, so an over-budget week turns them red until the parts shrink or the budget is raised.
